clue.text: Doctor Who includes ordinary lines and special craters

indicators.note: the rearranged word holds the next pieces inside it
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A sci-fi time traveller's adventure takes in ordinary lines and some special craters on an alien world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' looks like the TV hero, but 'Doctor' signals rearranging WHO into HOW, which 'includes' LL and O; S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollows are dips or depressions in the ground, much as craters are.

clue.text: Determines the position of in-store clobber

indicators.note: to clobber is to batter, so the letters of the hyphenated word get knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone working out where some in-store clothing is placed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like the British slang noun for clothes, but here it is a verb, meaning batter.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient something is to find or fix its position relative to surroundings.

indicators.note: the fib goes around the next pieces

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story, a fib

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A nobleman's tale concerns his estates' widening boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes the end letters E and G of 'expanding'; LIE goes 'about' them.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal superior or lord to whom vassals owe service.

clue.text: See top of wig — it's on head

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: the word it, with the 's read as a link meaning 'is'
a ness is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at the crown of a wig sitting on someone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to see it happen, as an onlooker does.

clue.text: Prepared food without recipe? That's wrong

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside: the cooked letters sit outside the next piece

parts.note: to have cooked is to have prepared food
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions (Latin recipe, take)

explanation.surface: Someone cooked a meal without following a recipe, and it went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but here means outside: COOKED wraps R.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked means dishonest or bent, so morally wrong.

clue.text: Struggle raising temperature on subsequent attempts

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a letter moves it higher, nearer the start of the word

parts.note: to resist is to struggle against

explanation.surface: A tough fight that pushes the temperature up, as in the heat of later tries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' lifts the T in RESIST up one place, giving the new word.
explanation.definitionFit: Resits are exams taken again after failing, so later attempts.

parts.note: 'stratospherically bad' reads as slang for extremely bad, but literally names a gap high up in the atmosphere's protective layer

explanation.surface: A green campaigner calling a problem off-the-scale terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stratospherically' as slang means hugely; taken literally it locates the problem in the stratosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The thinning of protective gas over Antarctica is a famous environmental problem found in the stratosphere.

parts.note: the word infinite printed with its last letter cut off, so it is itself a word missing its end, and it also means without limit

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is the word for limitless with its final E chopped: it shows its own meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without an end goes on forever, which is what infinite means.

indicators.note: read as a verb, designs means reshapes, so these letters are formed into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A tool built so as to guarantee a sharp design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designs' looks like a noun, but signals reworking ENSURING SHARP.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the gardener's tool, cutting blades for trimming branches.

definitions.note: crossword slang for a river, something with banks

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes inside the next piece

parts.note: Tyneside is in North East England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: the pound-and-one pair is read in reverse order

parts.note: L is the pound sign's letter (from libra) and I is the Roman one

explanation.surface: A bank employee returns a pound into a Newcastle account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' looks like a financier but is the crossword word for a river. £1 gives L and I, turned 'back' to IL, put 'into' NE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is an African river, and rivers are things with banks.

indicators.note: the words fall apart, their letters reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A tailoring note: the openings of a pair of shorts held apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Thresholds are doorways, entrances, so openings into a place or a start.

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name

indicators.note: to reject is to turn back, so the next letters are reversed

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A woman spurns her ex's side of the family or his political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' turns EX round to XE after ANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension built onto a building, like a wing.

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spoke at a rented building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun but is the verb, rearranging AT RENTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chatter, chat idly.

clue.text: They liquidate lots of tea at home in three seconds

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: Assam is a type of Indian tea

indicators.note: the at-home letters go inside the seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, three of them
IN means at home

explanation.surface: People who drink up gallons of tea at home in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquidate' looks like 'make liquid' but means kill. 'lots of' trims ASSAM to ASSA, and IN goes 'in' SSS as SS-IN-S.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidate someone is to kill them, so killers for hire liquidate their targets.

clue.text: God's first person in Australia gets English permit

indicators.note: the god and pronoun go inside the abbreviation for Australia

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A god's chosen one in Australia receives an English licence.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise is to give official permission, to sanction.

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England (there are several)

explanation.surface: A husband's riverside home.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a building people live in, a home.

indicators.note: the letters come out of the following words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: The close of one instalment of a three-part TV serial.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit within 'episoDE A THree-parter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Death is the end of life, the final close.

parts.note: ex means former
the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: Fluent ex-reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: To express something is to articulate it in words.

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A needy niece certainly goes hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurience is a rare, literary word for greed or hunger.

indicators.note: the reshaping is what makes the two words into the answer; these words point to rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone asking how to look older.
explanation.walkthrough: To make ME OLDER into a single word you rearrange its letters, which is exactly what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: To remodel is to rework or reshape, which is how you make one word from these letters.

clue.text: Sailor can jail band over onset of war

indicators.note: to jail is to lock up, so the can holds the following pieces inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the band goes over and around the following letter

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mariner may lock up a group over the start of hostilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onset of' gives W; REM goes 'over' (round) it, and the lot is 'jailed' in CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A crewman is a member of a ship's crew, a seaman.

indicators.note: letters that go bump are knocked about, so the word before is jumbled

explanation.surface: A child asking when the spooky noises in the dark happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls 'things that go bump in the night'; 'go bump' also jumbles THINGS, so the whole clue both builds and defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts are said to go bump in the dark hours after sunset, so that is when it happens.

clue.text: After surgery, confident 4's been removed on the other side

indicators.note: the next piece comes after the operation

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation

indicators.note: the numeral's letters are taken out of the confident word

parts.note: positive means confident, sure
IV is 4 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: After an operation, a patient's confidence goes missing on the far side.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4 down, but is IV, which is 'removed' from POSITIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opposite faces you from across the way, on the other side.

clue.text: Easily beat old steeplechaser going the wrong way

indicators.note: the horse's name is run backwards

parts.note: Red Rum was a famous racehorse, three times winner of the Grand National steeplechase in the 1970s

explanation.surface: Someone thrashing a past racehorse that ran the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is Britain's most famous Grand National winner; read backwards it is the answer (the twist from The Shining).
explanation.definitionFit: To murder an opponent is informal for beating them easily, thrashing them.

definitions.note: radio detection and ranging, a system for spotting distant objects

indicators.note: a word working both ways reads the same in either direction

parts.note: radio detection and ranging, a system for spotting distant objects

explanation.surface: A sensing system that works both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-way' looks like part of the description but says the answer reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar locates objects by bouncing radio waves off them, a detection system.

clue.text: At the start of a month, before bored doctor made out

parts.words: At the start of a month
parts.note: Dec I, the first of December, is the start of a month

indicators.note: the next word is pierced, with the old 'before' inside it

parts.note: a PhD is a doctor of philosophy
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: On the first of the month, a weary physician wrote something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored' looks like weary, but means drilled: ERE goes inside PHD.
explanation.definitionFit: To decipher writing is to make it out, work out what it says.

indicators.note: the last letter is docked

parts.note: Dumbo is the Disney elephant who flies with his ears

explanation.surface: Someone stunned into silence by seeing a cartoon elephant without its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb means unable or unwilling to speak, struck silent.

parts.note: the playwright's name splits as 'shake' plus SPEARE'S: shaking those seven letters gives a word for slander

explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal sits inside one word: 'shake' rearranges SPEARE'S, the rest of the Bard's name, and 'slander' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to cast slurs on someone, to defame or slander them.

clue.text: Strong iron forged into 50 small coins

parts.note: F is forte, loud or strong in music

indicators.note: the reshaped letters go inside the next pieces

parts.note: L is 50 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: metal that is forged is hammered into shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Tough iron is hammered into fifty little coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges IRON to ORIN, which goes 'into' L and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Florins were old British coins worth two shillings.
